title: QUIZ - 62
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Choose a clear, specific variable definition for a real-world quantity
questions.question: A model needs a variable (call it a) to represent the weight of packages shipped by a warehouse. Which variable definition is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Let a represent package weight.

options.label: B
options.text: Let a represent the total number of models.

options.label: C
options.text: Let a represent an unrelated fixed constant.

options.label: D
options.text: Let a represent the answer to the problem before it is solved.

questions.explanation: A variable should clearly and specifically represent the quantity that changes in the scenario, in this case package weight.
questions.hint: A well-defined variable clearly states what real-world quantity it represents, including units when relevant.

questions.learningObjective: Choose clear, distinct variable definitions for a two-quantity real-world scenario
questions.question: A problem involves the number of adult tickets and the number of child tickets sold. Which pair of variable definitions is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Let a = the total of both quantities and m = their difference.

options.label: B
options.text: Let a = child tickets sold and m = an unrelated constant.

options.label: C
options.text: Let a and m both represent adult tickets sold.

options.label: D
options.text: Let a = adult tickets sold and m = child tickets sold.

questions.explanation: Each variable should represent one distinct, specific quantity: a for adult tickets sold and m for child tickets sold.
questions.hint: Each variable should represent exactly one clearly identified, distinct quantity.

options.label: C

questions.learningObjective: Critique an imprecise variable definition and explain why it is ambiguous
questions.question: A student defines a variable as "let n = the cost." Why is this definition potentially problematic for building an accurate model?

options.label: A
options.text: It does not specify the units or exactly which cost (e.g., cost per item, total cost, or cost per hour) is meant.

options.label: B
options.text: Cost cannot be represented by a variable in any mathematical model.

options.label: C
options.text: The definition is stated in a complete sentence, which is not allowed.

options.label: D
options.text: It uses the letter n, which cannot be used as a variable in algebra.

questions.explanation: A precise variable definition should specify exactly what is being measured and in what units, avoiding ambiguity between, for example, cost per item, total cost, or cost per hour.
questions.hint: Consider whether the definition leaves any ambiguity about what exactly is being measured.

options.label: C
options.text: Distance cannot be represented by a variable in any mathematical model.

options.label: D
options.text: The definition is stated in a complete sentence, which is not allowed.

questions.explanation: A precise variable definition should specify exactly what is being measured and in what units, avoiding ambiguity between, for example, distance per trip, total distance traveled, or distance remaining.
questions.hint: Consider whether the definition leaves any ambiguity about what exactly is being measured.
